segments.arabic: [1069] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا سليمان بن أبي مسلم عن طاوس سمع ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Abi Muslim related to us, from Tawus, who heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا قام من الليل يتهجد قال اللهم لك الحمد أنت قيم السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن ولك الحمد لك ملك السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن ولك الحمد أنت نور السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن ولك الحمد أنت ملك السماوات والأرض ولك الحمد أنت الحق ووعدك الحق ولقاؤك حق وقولك حق والجنة حق والنار حق والنبيون حق ومحمد ﷺ حق والساعة حق اللهم لك أسلمت وبك آمنت وعليك توكلت وإليك أنبت وبك خاصمت وإليك حاكمت فاغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت وما أسررت وما أعلنت أنت المقدم وأنت المؤخر لا إله إلا أنت أو لا إله غيرك
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he rose during the night for tahajjud, would say: “O Allah, to You belongs praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. Yours is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. You are the King of the heavens and the earth. To You belongs praise. You are the Truth. Your promise is the truth; meeting You is true; Your word is true; Paradise is true; the Fire is true; the prophets are true; Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is true; and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, on You I have relied, and to You I have turned. By You I have argued, and to You I have brought my case for judgment. Forgive me what I have done earlier and later, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back. There is no god except You,” or, “There is no god other than You.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان وزاد عبد الكريم أبو أمية ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
segments.english: Sufyan said: ‘Abd al-Karim Abu Umayyah added, “And there is no power and no strength except through Allah.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان قال سليمان بن أبي مسلم سمعه من طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Sufyan said: Sulayman ibn Abi Muslim said that he heard it from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

comparisons.note: The light clause lacks the selected words about those within the heavens and earth, and the separate King clause is absent. The closing Sufyan/Sulayman route is abbreviated.

checkedBody: When the Prophet got up at night to offer the Tahajjud prayer, he used to say: Allahumma lakal-hamd. Anta qaiyimus-samawati wal-ard wa man fihinna. Walakal-hamd, Laka mulkus-samawati wal-ard wa man fihinna. Walakal-hamd, anta nurus-samawati wal-ard. Walakalhamd, anta-l-haq wa wa'duka-l-haq, wa liqa'uka Haq, wa qualuka Haq, wal-jannatu Han wan-naru Haq wannabiyuna Haq. Wa Muhammadun, sallal-lahu'alaihi wasallam, Haq, was-sa'atu Haq. Allahumma aslamtu Laka wabika amantu, wa 'Alaika tawakkaltu, wa ilaika anabtu wa bika khasamtu, wa ilaika hakamtu faghfir li ma qaddamtu wama akh-khartu wama as-rartu wama'a lantu, anta-l-muqaddim wa anta-l-mu akh-khir, la ilaha illa anta (or la ilaha ghairuka). (O Allah! All the praises are for you, You are the Holder of the Heavens and the Earth, And whatever is in them. All the praises are for You; You have the possession of the Heavens and the Earth And whatever is in them. All the praises are for You; You are the Light of the Heavens and the Earth And all the praises are for You; You are the King of the Heavens and the Earth; And all the praises are for You; You are the Truth and Your Promise is the truth, And to meet You is true, Your Word is the truth And Paradise is true And Hell is true And all the Prophets (Peace be upon them) are true; And Muhammad is true, And the Day of Resurrection is true. O Allah ! I surrender (my will) to You; I believe in You and depend on You. And repent to You, And with Your help I argue (with my opponents, the non-believers) And I take You as a judge (to judge between us). Please forgive me my previous And future sins; And whatever I concealed or revealed And You are the One who make (some people) forward And (some) backward. There is none to be worshipped but you . Sufyan said that 'Abdul Karim Abu Umaiya added to the above, 'Wala haula Wala quwata illa billah' (There is neither might nor power except with Allah).
comparisons.note: The transliteration and English are not identical in scope: the separate King clause appears only in the English, and the selected closing Sufyan/Sulayman/Tawus route is absent. The transliteration also has a Han spelling at the Paradise truth clause.

notes: Retain every repeated praise clause, both no-god alternatives and both closing Sufyan comments. Historical praise order differs; comparison English is not a substitute for the selected Arabic.

Every repeated praise clause, including the separate King clause and all three those-within-them phrases, remains in the selected order. The two no-god alternatives and both Sufyan notes remain separate and complete.

Sustainer renders قيم; By You I have argued and brought my case for judgment retain the argument/adjudication expressions without importing the comparison’s opponent, unbeliever or sin glosses. These theological and lexical choices require independent review.
The final Sufyan note explicitly preserves Sulayman’s hearing from Tawus. The Abd al-Karim addition remains an attributed transmission note; it is not merged into the preceding prayer.

segments.arabic: [1070] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا هشام قال: أخبرنا معمر وحدثني محمود قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري عن سالم عن أبيه رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us. And Mahmud related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: كان الرجل في حياة النبي ﷺ إذا رأى رؤيا قصها على رسول الله ﷺ فتمنيت أن أرى رؤيا فأقصها على رسول الله ﷺ وكنت غلاما شابا وكنت أنام في المسجد على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فرأيت في النوم كأن ملكين أخذاني فذهبا بي إلى النار فإذا هي مطوية كطي البئر وإذا لها قرنان وإذا فيها أناس قد عرفتهم فجعلت أقول أعوذ بالله من النار قال: فلقينا ملك آخر، فقال لي لم ترع
segments.english: During the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when a man saw a dream, he would recount it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I wished to see a dream so that I could recount it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I was a young man, and I used to sleep in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. In my sleep I saw as though two angels took me and brought me to the Fire. It was built around like the lining of a well, and it had two uprights. There were people in it whom I recognized. I began saying, “I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.” He said: Then another angel met us and said to me, “You need not be afraid.”

segments.arabic: فقصصتها على حفصة فقصتها حفصة على رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: نعم الرجل عبد الله لو كان يصلي من الليل فكان بعد لا ينام من الليل إلا قليلا
segments.english: I recounted it to Hafsah, and Hafsah recounted it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, “What a fine man ‘Abdullah is! If only he prayed during the night.” After that, he slept only a little during the night.

comparisons.note: The later figure is rendered as another man, while the selected Arabic and both inspected prints say another angel.

notes: Two opening routes and the complete dream/Hafsah account are present. The modern edition divides this single digital paragraph into 1121 and 1122; neither is missing.

The two opening routes through Hisham/Mamar and Mahmud/Abd al-Razzaq/Mamar remain complete. Related to me in the second route is singular. Modern printed 1121 and 1122 remain in one complete digital entry.

The well-lining and two-uprights renderings follow the lexical discussion in Ibn Hajar; no wood, stone, named dream figures or religious interpretation is added. The selected other angel is retained rather than the web comparison’s man. The closing he is not replaced by an inserted attribution to Salim.

segments.arabic: [1071] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أخبرته
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي إحدى عشرة ركعة كانت تلك صلاته يسجد السجدة من ذلك قدر ما يقرأ أحدكم خمسين آية قبل أن يرفع رأسه ويركع ركعتين قبل صلاة الفجر ثم يضطجع على شقه الأيمن حتى يأتيه المنادي للصلاة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray eleven rak‘ahs. That was his prayer. In it, he would remain in a prostration for as long as one of you would take to recite fifty verses before raising his head. He would pray two rak‘ahs before the Fajr prayer, then lie down on his right side until the caller came to him for the prayer.

notes: The eleven-unit report, fifty-verse comparison, two Fajr units and right-side rest remain together.
Eleven rakahs, fifty verses, the two before Fajr, right-side resting and the arriving caller all remain. The two before Fajr are not retitled with an inserted Sunnah parenthesis.

segments.arabic: [1072] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا سفيان عن الأسود قال: سمعت جندبا يقول
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aswad, who said: I heard Jundub say:

segments.arabic: اشتكى النبي ﷺ فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill and did not rise for one night or two.

notes: Retain the one-or-two-night uncertainty; this is a separate Jundub occurrence.
The one-night-or-two uncertainty remains. No cause of illness or definite duration is supplied.

segments.arabic: [1073] حدثنا محمد بن كثير قال: أخبرنا سفيان عن الأسود بن قيس عن جندب بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundub ibn ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: احتبس جبريل ﷺ على النبي ﷺ فقالت امرأة من قريش أبطأ عليه شيطانه فنزلت { والضحى والليل إذا سجى ما ودعك ربك وما قلى }
segments.english: Jibril, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delayed in coming to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. A woman of Quraysh said, “His devil has been slow in coming to him.” Then it was revealed: “By the morning brightness, and by the night when it grows still: your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.”

checkedBody: Gabriel did not come to the Prophet (for some time) and so one of the Quraish women said, "His Satan has deserted him." So came the Divine Revelation: "By the forenoon And by the night When it is still! Your Lord (O Muhammad) has neither Forsaken you Nor hated you." (93.1-3)
comparisons.note: The woman’s statement is rendered as deserted rather than the selected delay wording.

notes: Retain both Gabriel and Prophet honorifics and the exact quoted Quran endpoint; this is distinct from the preceding illness report.

Both source blessings, including the one attached to Jibril, remain. The Qurayshi woman is unnamed. Her words refer to delay, not the English comparison’s stronger deserted. The embedded Quran passage is a provisional translation of the exact selected words; verse numbers stay outside the report.

segments.arabic: [1074] حدثنا ابن مقاتل أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري عن هند بنت الحارث عن أم سلمة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Ibn Muqatil related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ استيقظ ليلة، فقال سبحان الله ماذا أنزل الليلة من الفتنة ماذا أنزل من الخزائن من يوقظ صواحب الحجرات يا رب كاسية في الدنيا عارية في الآخرة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke one night and said, “Glory be to Allah! What has been sent down tonight of trial! What has been sent down of treasures! Who will wake the women of the chambers? How many a woman is clothed in this world but naked in the Hereafter!”

comparisons.note: The selected question about who will wake the occupants is rendered as an instruction to go and wake them.

checkedBody: One night the Prophet got up and said, "Subhan Allah! How many afflictions Allah has revealed tonight and how many treasures have been sent down (disclosed). Go and wake the sleeping lady occupants of these dwellings up (for prayers), perhaps a well-dressed in this world may be naked in the Hereafter."
comparisons.note: The selected question about who will wake the occupants is rendered as an instruction, with added prayer and sleeping explanations.

notes: The affliction, treasure, question about the occupants and clothing clauses remain complete. The English comparisons turn the question into an imperative.

Who will wake remains a question, not the imperative in both English comparisons. No Allah-as-agent, sleeping, for-prayers or identity parenthesis is inserted. How many a woman renders the feminine idiom يا رب كاسية; it does not turn the statement into a generic person.

segments.arabic: [1075] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني علي بن حسين أن حسين بن علي أخبره أن علي بن أبي طالب أخبره
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ali ibn Husayn informed me that Husayn ibn ‘Ali informed him that ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ طرقه وفاطمة بنت النبي عليه السلام ليلة، فقال ألا تصليان فقلت: يا رسول الله أنفسنا بيد الله فإذا شاء أن يبعثنا بعثنا فانصرف حين قلنا ذلك ولم يرجع إلي شيئا ثم سمعته وهو مول يضرب فخذه وهو يقول { وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا }
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him and Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet, peace be upon him, one night and said, “Will you two not pray?” I said, “Messenger of Allah, our souls are in Allah’s hand. If He wills to raise us, He raises us.” He turned away when we said that and gave me no reply. Then I heard him, as he was turning away, striking his thigh and saying, “Man is, more than anything, argumentative.”

notes: Retain the full Ali/Husayn route, night visit, response, departure, thigh action and exact Quran excerpt.

The entire Ali ibn Husayn/Husayn ibn Ali/Ali ibn Abi Talib chain remains. The report retains its shift from him to I, the two-person question, we said versus gave me no reply, the hand expression and the thigh action. The selected second honorific is peace be upon him, not the longer blessing. The Quran quotation remains exact in scope.

segments.arabic: [1076] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: إن كان رسول الله ﷺ ليدع العمل وهو يحب أن يعمل به خشية أن يعمل به الناس فيفرض عليهم وما سبح رسول الله ﷺ سبحة الضحى قط وإني لأسبحها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would leave an action although he loved to do it, fearing that people would act upon it and it would be made obligatory for them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never offered the Duha prayer, but I do offer it.

notes: Retain the concern about obligation and both Duha statements without importing a legal explanation.

The selected never-offered-Duha statement remains without reconciling it with other reports. This is a translation of the selected account, not an inferred ruling. Both Messenger honorifics are retained.

segments.arabic: [1077] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ صلى ذات ليلة في المسجد فصلى بصلاته ناس ثم صلى من القابلة فكثر الناس ثم اجتمعوا من الليلة الثالثة أو الرابعة فلم يخرج إليهم رسول الله ﷺ فلما أصبح قال قد رأيت الذي صنعتم ولم يمنعني من الخروج إليكم إلا أني خشيت أن تفرض عليكم وذلك في رمضان
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one night in the mosque, and some people followed his prayer. Then he prayed on the following night, and the people grew in number. Then they gathered on the third or fourth night, but the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out to them. When morning came, he said, “I saw what you did. Nothing prevented me from coming out to you except my fear that it would be made obligatory for you.” That was in Ramadan.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Aisha, the mother of the faithful believers:

One night Allah's Apostle offered the prayer in the Mosque and the people followed him. The next night he also offered the prayer and too many people gathered. On the third and the fourth nights more people gathered, but Allah's Apostle did not come out to them. In the morning he said, "I saw what you were doing and nothing but the fear that it (i.e. the prayer) might be enjoined on you, stopped me from coming to you." And that happened in the month of Ramadan.
comparisons.damagedExcerpt: On the third and the fourth nights
comparisons.note: The selected third or fourth night becomes third and fourth nights.

notes: Retain third or fourth uncertainty, the morning explanation and Ramadan ending.

Mother of the Believers is retained in the opening. The selected third-or-fourth uncertainty is not changed to the EPUB’s third-and-fourth. The closing Ramadan clause stays outside the direct quotation.

segments.arabic: [1078] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا مسعر عن زياد قال: سمعت المغيرة رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us, from Ziyad, who said: I heard al-Mughirah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

segments.arabic: إن كان النبي ﷺ ليقوم ليصلي حتى ترم قدماه أو ساقاه فيقال له فيقول أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand to pray until his feet or his lower legs swelled. When this was mentioned to him, he would say, “Should I not be a thankful servant?”

segments.arabic: [1079] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا عمرو بن دينار أن عمرو بن أوس أخبره أن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضى الله تعالى عنهما أخبره
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us that ‘Amr ibn Aws informed him that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال له أحب الصلاة إلى الله صلاة داود عليه السلام وأحب الصيام إلى الله صيام داود وكان ينام نصف الليل ويقوم ثلثه وينام سدسه ويصوم يوما ويفطر يوما
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “The prayer most beloved to Allah is the prayer of Dawud, peace be upon him, and the fasting most beloved to Allah is the fasting of Dawud. He used to sleep half the night, stand for a third of it, and sleep a sixth of it. He would fast one day and not fast the next.”

notes: The half/third/sixth divisions and alternate-day fasting remain exact, with the source honorifics.

Both most-beloved clauses and all three night fractions remain. Only the first Dawud occurrence has the source peace honorific; no second honorific is inserted. Standing is not expanded with extra prayer details.

segments.arabic: [1080] حدثني عبدان قال: أخبرني أبي عن شعبة عن أشعث سمعت أبي قال: سمعت مسروقا قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to me. He said: My father informed me, from Shu‘bah, from Ash‘ath, who said: I heard my father say: I heard Masruq say:

segments.arabic: سألت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أي العمل كان أحب إلى النبي ﷺ قالت الدائم قلت: متى كان يقوم قالت يقوم إذا سمع الصارخ
segments.english: I asked ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, “Which action was most beloved to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” She said, “That which is constant.” I asked, “When would he rise?” She said, “He would rise when he heard the rooster.”

notes: The complete Masruq question-and-answer account occupies the first part of printed 1132.

Both distinct my father links remain in the chain, one from Abdan and one from Ashath. The I asked Aishah framing stays visible with its questions. The rooster is the lexical referent of الصارخ according to Ibn Hajar; no time of night is supplied.

segments.arabic: [1082] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد قال: ذكر أبي عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت

segments.arabic: [1083] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا روح قال: حدثنا سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Rawh related to us. He said: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن نبي الله ﷺ وزيد بن ثابت رضى الله تعالى عنه تسحرا فلما فرغا من سحورهما قام نبي الله ﷺ إلى الصلاة فصلى قلنا لأنس كم كان بين فراغهما من سحورهما ودخولهما في الصلاة قال كقدر ما يقرأ الرجل خمسين آية
segments.english: The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, ate suhur. When they had finished their suhur, the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose for the prayer and prayed. We asked Anas, “How long was there between their finishing suhur and their entering the prayer?” He said, “As long as a man takes to recite fifty verses.”

notes: Retain both the meal/prayer account and the later question to Anas with its fifty-verse answer.

The original says we asked Anas; Qatadah is not inserted as a new speaking attribution. All three source blessings, the dual suhur/prayer references and fifty verses remain. The report does not supply Fajr, morning or Quran parenthetical wording.

segments.arabic: [1084] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأعمش عن أبي وائل عن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع النبي ﷺ ليلة فلم يزل قائما حتى هممت بأمر سوء قلنا وما هممت قال هممت أن أقعد وأذر النبي ﷺ
segments.english: I prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night. He remained standing until I considered doing something bad. We asked, “What did you consider?” He said, “I considered sitting down and leaving the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: Retain both the long standing account and the question clarifying the intended action.
The narrator is Abdullah as written, without an added ibn Masud. The we asked exchange and both Prophet blessings remain. Something bad is not presented as a separate legal classification.
